how: The starter proposes the M and locates its anchor, with subsequent joining treated separately under the revised definition.
Members call for more people through class Facebook groups while asking them to erase an opponent.
A request for mutual help receives a bare joining commitment.
Moderators consolidate canvas posts into a megathread and redirect later requests to the sticky.
Participants propose the M, consider widening it, add an inscription, and alter letter widths to fit.
Participants commit to seeding the M and report completion of the mark, border, and widening.
Coordinates and an official template guide placing while participants appeal for adherence to the original plan.
Members request bot code and report bots maintaining several logos including their own.
Participants repair stray changes, guard the work, and put defence before growth or redesign.
Apply the repair-away explanation only where rejected changes are attributable to uninformed keepers, since coordination complaints alone do not establish that cause.
Neighbours discuss non-vandalism, room-sharing, relocation assistance, and protection bargains.
Participants prohibit attacks on college neighbours and apologise for taking another group's area.
Requests for help produce joining commitments, thanks, reciprocal assurances, conditions, and refusals.
Participants call for a common college corner and shared logo while debating the alliance's scope.
Offering rebuilding room does not establish an ongoing guest arrangement governed by the host.
A member reports carrying a relocation-and-help offer to another room in Spanish.
Disagreement over alliance membership does not identify who may commit other placers or explicitly limit an envoy's standing.
Participants call for altering rival lettering, wiping another school out, and finishing a rival off together.
Participants claim joint victory and recount wars they say they won.
A builder attributes erased work to a neighbouring flag that threatens half the M.
School names and hostility during the event do not independently document a specific quarrel predating the canvas.
Attack calls name school opponents and invoke league membership as an exclusion boundary.
A participant judges enlargement too risky because too few people are online.
Dropping a proposed inscription site and reporting another group's move do not establish relocation of the room's lost home.
Members celebrate completion, congratulate builders, and credit their own guarding labour.
Participants propose a development history, announce the end, and recount how the work fared.
Recounting completed work and guarding does not show a decision to sustain the collective or continue elsewhere.
Post-finish fault-finding does not establish a cleanup request, correction of a historical claim, or contest over a preserved copy.
Members recognise an April Fools logo prank, report being fooled, and preserve the reveal.
Members invoke shared college affiliation and distinguish their school from a neighbouring ally.
An organiser's self-description and posting moderation do not establish selected canvas command or test the cross-room prevalence claim.
A member proposes starting a coordination chat to gather people for an inscription threatened by a neighbour.
Treat deliberation over starting a chat as a proposal unless evidence establishes actual migration or decisions made there.
A reported Spanish negotiation is not evidence of concealing strategy or infiltrating another venue.
A participant corrects which school is involved in the live defence discussion.
Outside help requests establish visitors but do not identify the mark as their route into the room.
Congratulating builders does not establish seeking recognition from represented outsiders or the press.
Participants locate an anchor, consider neighbouring claims, and propose abandoning an additional inscription site.
The completion title uses a comic label without establishing the linked image's appearance or a shared running joke.
An existing room's project and a chat proposal do not establish formation of a new community around a mark.
Recorded profanity and refusals do not establish an exchange policing slurs or offensive canvas jokes.
A participant questions excluding a rival while another apologises for taking a neighbour's area, without articulating a general philosophy of covering.
Redirecting canvas requests to a sticky does not establish a host member attacking the room's mark in protest.
Accepting a practical pause does not establish personal distress, withdrawal under strain, or repair of an interpersonal quarrel.
Members report occasional checking and overnight guarding without documenting specific lost sleep or other personal costs.
Wrong-placement complaints and contradictory messages do not identify a site fault or tested fix in the existing concepts.
Choosing to support an allied school does not establish belonging to both rooms or divided allegiance.
The initial M proposal supplies an existing project for later calls to build its inscription.
A supplied coordinate is followed by an explicit commitment to place the seed pixel of the proposed mark.
A direct request receives a bare acceptance without demonstrating silent placement or the proposed general preference mechanism.
Consolidation and redirection are explicit, but the coded passages do not identify a recruitment-caused flood as their motive.
A posted template settles practice only insofar as builders receive and follow its current version.
Reported completion is followed by explicit commitments to maintain the standing design.
Perceived opposing automation motivates requesting code without independently establishing exhaustion of manual upkeep capacity.
A perceived neighbouring flag threat is followed by an explicit relocation-and-help offer without proof that the offer caused retreat.
Cooperation is invoked to discourage attacks, but the concepts do not identify a settled border causing compliance.
Maintenance-related requests yield help only when participants accept the exchange, which can depend on a protection guarantee.
A withdrawal and proposed trade must remain distinguishable from completed aid because requests can be refused.
A defence appeal is followed by an explicit call for common affiliation to unite against the threat.
One recruitment call directly asks for more people and erasure of an opponent.
A renewed exclusion call receives a direct bare question challenging whether the rival should instead be allowed space.
A treaty includes attack and restoration, but the concepts do not establish an attack call causing subsequent negotiation.
Calls to finish a rival are followed by claims of a joint victory over that rival.
Reporting completion and celebrating it can occur within the same passage rather than separate turns.
A history proposal and completion congratulations show recording beside celebration without establishing the proposed causal transition.
The history proposal and retrospective account do not show an ensuing decision to sustain the temporary collective.
Too few hands for enlargement does not establish the narrower antecedent of being unable to hold an overrun home.
The agreement and disagreement concepts do not document refusal of binding authority after agreement or express limits stated while making terms.
Updating public instructions can follow successful haphazard construction rather than settle all placing in advance.
A treaty can combine eliminating a third party with mutual restoration rather than make negotiation an alternative to attack.
Shared affiliation produces a coalition only to the extent participants accept it despite narrower loyalties and continued internal fighting.
